items.title: A chart component library, shared by all eight surfaces
items.detail: `public/shared/charts.js` (640 lines) exists with all five named primitives plus `sparkline` and the scale helpers, and is exercised by `test/charts.test.js` (50 tests). It is imported by 2 of 8 surfaces — `public/co/app.js:11` (static) and `public/app.js:1010` (lazy) — and only `barChart`, `sparkline` and `smallMultiples` have call sites anywhere outside the library; `lineChart`, `stackedBar` and `heatmap` have none.
items.note: public/shared/charts.js with lineChart, barChart, stackedBar, heatmap, sparkline, smallMultiples, legend, caption and divergingBar — the last because scenarios drew a two-pixel div bar and approximating it with barChart loses the zero anchor. 206 tests across the charts and viz suites. All primitives return SVG strings, take no DOM and are used by every surface that draws.

items.title: Render uncertainty as geometry, not as a footnote
items.detail: `lineChart` can draw an uncertainty band (`public/shared/charts.js:232-256`) and two tests guard it, but `lineChart` has zero call sites outside its own test file — no chart in the product passes `low`/`high`. There is no `not_included` caption anywhere in `public/` or `src/`, and no map uncertainty mode: no confidence-driven opacity or hatch exists in `public/app.js`.
items.note: public/shared/viz-uncertainty.js. sensitivityBandChart draws the band HATCHED, never as a gradient — a soft ribbon is the confidence-interval visual grammar and hatching survives greyscale and colour blindness. Edge labels read 'sensitivity low'/'sensitivity high'; a test asserts p10, p90 and 'percentile' appear nowhere in the SVG, table or caption. The disclaimer is in the return value, not an option, so the wiring step copies the geometry and the sentence together, and a record claiming `calibrated_uncertainty: true` throws rather than being relabelled. Rendered on the console over 16 live risk records, with the module's own caption verbatim beneath.

items.title: Time-slider playback of hazard history
items.detail: No scrubber, play/pause or speed control in any surface. A search for `input type="range"`, `scrub` and `playback` across `public/` returns nothing; the only `setInterval` uses are the 30s queue flush (`public/shared/runtime.js:172`) and the console's self-rescheduling poll (`public/app.js:4176`), neither of which replays hazard frames.
items.note: public/shared/viz-playback.js. The console steps 292 hazard events and 10 alert events through buildFrames, auto-bucketed to weeks over a 364-day span, with frameSummary per frame and peakFrame for a 'Jump to peak (2026-09-28, 69 active)' control. The chart discloses that 68 of 78 records carry no end date and stay active for the rest of the timeline — so a rising count is the archive accumulating, not floods worsening.

items.title: Map → chart → record drill-down, with a `/explain` endpoint
items.detail: No `/api/v1/explain/:kind/:id` route exists — the route table in `src/server.js` has no matching path. A map click opens `openDetailDialog` (`public/app.js:3781`), which renders the record's own fields as a flat `<dl>` — no time series, no underlying records, no per-term coefficient breakdown. The adjacent evidence defect did get fixed: `calibrationReport` is now routed from `/api/v1/assessments` (`src/server.js:1276`), but that is the calibration metadata, not the equation endpoint.
items.note: Every record the console opens now explains itself: map markers, map record list, alert rows. `explainRecord` (public/shared/viz-explain.js) renders the arithmetic; GET /api/v1/explain/{id} supplies the provenance the client cannot compute — the source run and the lineage row. A record naming no source run returns 200 with `provenance.known: false` and a sentence saying so, because absence of provenance is a fact about the record, not a reason to withhold it.

items.title: Month × year seasonal calendar heatmap
items.detail: The `heatmap` primitive exists and is tested (`test/charts.test.js:264-319`) but has no call site outside the library. No surface builds a month×year matrix, nothing computes departure from a climatological median, and there is no flood/alert overlay on a grid. `public/shared/seasonal.js` still has exactly one consumer, `public/app.js:7`, which renders the single-summary strip.
items.note: The month×year matrix is on the console with the flood/alert overlay the item asks for: 78 hazard and alert records bucketed to months across the ENSO grid's own columns. It is a calendar rather than a single anomaly number because the structure an operator reads for is seasonal — a warm phase peaks around November-December and decays through the following spring. It does NOT difference against a per-month climatological median: the published anomaly is already a departure from a 30-year base, and differencing twice reports the spread of the series under study rather than its position. It does not interpolate an un-ingested month.

items.title: Forecast-versus-observed verification charts
items.detail: No reliability diagram, no forecast-probability binning, no lead-time axis anywhere in `src/` or `public/`; `lead_time_days` appears only as a fixture field (`test/lite.test.js:127`) and a display string in `public/workflow/ops.js:43`. `src/analytics/ensemble.js` remains dead: `computeEnsembleStats` is called only from itself and from tests, and both connectors still write `ensemble_p10/p50/p90: null`.
items.note: public/shared/viz-verify.js. pairForecasts joins 54 precipitation_forecast records against flattened archive dailies on region-day; reliability and reliabilityDiagram render the result. **The store holds zero archive records, so all 54 pairs are `pending` (28) or `no_outcome` (26) and none is verified.** The console renders 'Not yet measured' with the per-status counts, why the gap is missing outcomes rather than a good result, and the event definition it will use — and draws no diagram. An honest empty state is the deliverable here; a chart of invented data would not be.

items.title: Offline-first drill-down and cached map tiles
items.detail: Three of the five changes shipped: the precache list is now a computed breadth-first closure of the real import graph (`public/sw.js:111`, guarded by `test/web-chw-offline.test.js:437-513`); the queue throws unless IndexedDB confirms the write (`public/shared/runtime.js:66-95`, `submitOrQueue` at `:251`, guarded by 12 tests); and `/api/v1/*` GETs are network-first with an API cache fallback and an `x-lindela-offline` header (`public/sw.js:210-240`, read at `public/shared/runtime.js:217`) under a tested eviction cap. Missing: there is no tile cache of any kind in `public/sw.js`, and no "last synced" indicator — no surface reads the offline header or renders per-panel staleness.
items.note: Three read buckets in the service worker: a named record gets its own (60 entries, 7-day TTL) so the console's 30-second poll cannot evict the districts a health worker visited; the map's hazard/flood/road layers get a third (48, 2-day). basemap.js is inline polygons and fetches nothing, so there are no tiles to cache. A miss is never an empty panel: 503 with a code, and `cached: false` distinguishes 'no data' from 'no data because I never fetched any'. Hits carry x-lindela-stored-at and x-lindela-stale-seconds stamped when written, not read off Date. Two defects fixed en route: activate would have deleted the detail bucket on every version bump, and stale hits were rewrapped under the stored response's own content-encoding.

items.title: Colourblind-safe and high-contrast themes
items.detail: The secondary-encoding half shipped and is guarded: `hazardShape` (`public/app.js:1356`) and `severityDash` (`public/app.js:1373`) are applied to every map and legend severity class, with six tests in `test/web-console.test.js:214-262` asserting distinct shapes, distinct dash patterns and that an ungraded record is not painted as "low". The palette half did not: `public/tokens.css` is a single dark `:root` with no deuteranopia/protanopia/tritanopia check, no high-contrast mode, and no `prefers-contrast`/`forced-colors` theme; `scripts/check-a11y.mjs:24` audits WCAG contrast but only against that one theme.
items.note: [data-theme] on <html>, applied purely at the token layer: `:root, :root[data-theme=dark]` keeps the shipped palette, plus light, high-contrast, and two @media mirrors that are the only correct path at first paint. Precedence is explicit choice > prefers-contrast > prefers-color-scheme > dark, persisted, with localStorage throwing degrading to 'no preference'. check-a11y measures all three themes across all eight surfaces — 24 assertions, all passing — and applies each theme the way a choice actually arrives, by writing localStorage before the page script. Colour-vision separation simulated (Machado 2009, severity 1.0): worst pairwise CIE76 dE dark 8.7, light 7.4, contrast 10.0. Severity carries word + glyph + a hatch whose density rises with severity, so nothing depends on hue alone.

items.title: Shareable, deep-linked, per-role dashboard state
items.detail: The console encodes and restores six filter/time-window params — `sev`, `source`, `range`, `cold`, `alerts`, `workflow` — through `syncFiltersToUrl`/`restoreFiltersFromUrl` (`public/app.js:2867-2921`), called from 5 sites including boot at `:4185`; scenarios has a share token in the URL hash plus a copy button. Missing: map extent and selected feature are not in the URL, there is no per-role saved default view anywhere (`public/shared/runtime.js` exports no view-config API), and no test exercises any of it — the only `replaceState` reference in `test/` is a stub. Shipped, unguarded.
items.note: public/shared/view-state.js, pure and testable, so a share link can be asserted without a browser. Three properties a URL has to have, because a link is a claim about what someone was looking at: the encoding is deterministic (map transforms are floats, and a link that differed per run would copy something the sender never saw); fields equal to the role default are not written, so a link narrows a role default rather than overwriting it; and it is versioned, with a link from a newer build decoding its known fields and carrying an advisory. ROLE_DEFAULTS covers seven roles. The share button appears only once the view differs from the default. Round trip verified in a browser. test/view-state.test.js, 17 tests.
